expectedObservation: The active _Concurrency.swiftinterface inventory is generated and every mechanically exposed group member and overload has an explicit implementation/verification disposition with positive evidence or an owned negative/deferral rationale.
currentObservation: The generated inventory retains every active task-group overload plus all six public TaskGroup.Iterator and ThrowingTaskGroup.Iterator next/cancel rows with effect/isolation metadata. All seventy-seven generated task-group and iterator rows now have authored dispositions: the four public scope rows; state, cancelAll, canonical addTask/addTaskUnlessCancelled, named add, executor-preference add/addUnless, immediate add/addUnless, deprecated aliases, makeAsyncIterator, next, and iterator cancel declarations are all accounted. Same-source native parity covers the default-isolation scope-function subsets, the supported nonisolated ordinary-add subsets, conditional acceptance before cancellation and rejection afterward, iterator value semantics and terminal states, waitForAll, nextResult, and Task.name preservation. Strict Swift 6 probes select each named, executor-preference, conditional, and immediate overload family. For all eight immediate declarations, the explicit-nil inherited-MainActor subset matches Swift's guaranteed causal behavior: an operation starts synchronously before its add call returns, resumes after forced suspension, preserves Task.name, and is joined at scope exit; an active conditional call returns true, while a call after cancelAll returns false without creating the child and before preference validation. No sibling finish order or physical-thread behavior is claimed. Shared runtime guards reject active non-nil TaskExecutor preferences instead of silently ignoring them, but native CountingTaskExecutor evidence proves preference-driven resumption is observable. The sixteen ordinary executor-preference rows and eight immediate rows therefore remain known divergences together with arbitrary @isolated(any) operation-executor behavior. Pinned swiftlang inputs independently anchor ordinary group behavior; start-immediately inputs provide semantic and compile provenance but their task-group executor block is disabled, so local same-source runtime evidence remains authoritative. No currently generated task-group overload is unreviewed. Repeated wait/new-work semantics, task-executor preference scheduling, and arbitrary actor executors stay open and are demand-deferred (2026-07-16): they have zero measured demand across the 669-project corpus and FoodTruck and reopen only when a real interpreted program fails on a cited declaration.

currentObservation: Synchronous actor initializers are characterized as lexically nonisolated while seeding their new instance; the first subsequent isolated method owns the registered mailbox and final release removes the actor record. A task-local binding remains attached to one logical task through actor entry, suspension/reacquisition, and dynamic-scope restoration while each actor segment owns the mailbox. Synchronous and async actor-isolated functions plus externally awaited synchronous computed-property/subscript getters and async computed/subscript getters now enter through runtime-owned mailbox leases; isolated parameters select that same executor from an explicit source actor or from a default #isolation value inherited from a source actor, MainActor, or a struct-/enum-backed custom global actor whose shared value has an arbitrary source-actor type, while explicit nil and a nonisolated caller's nil default remain nonisolated; canonical waits release the complete nested segment and reacquire it before resumption; unawaited cross-actor function/computed-getter/subscript-getter/isolated-parameter entry and eager async-computed/subscript-getter entry in canonical async sessions fail closed unless a supported suspending path is used; computed-property and subscript setters require an already-owned segment and external mutation is rejected by compiler preflight; and mutable stored-property funnels require the matching lease. Cross-actor throwing/cancellation-observing functions and successful, source-throwing, or cancelled async computed/subscript getters release the target and restore the caller before subsequent caller work. Replayable seeded mailbox stress proves ownership and complete runtime draining across varied fanout, rounds, and suspension patterns. Queued-message cancellation and the remaining unsupported-form audit are still open; per the 2026-07-16 demand re-plan the remaining fail-closed flips stay staged per feature instead of landing as an up-front global rejection.
